answer: In a trust-weighted attestation graph, each verifier is a beacon and bounded-length random walks diffuse credibility only across reachable, well-supported edges. A Sybil cluster can inflate internal links, but its sparse external cut has low conductance, so min-cut transitivity bounds the probability mass—and thus aggregate voting weight—that escapes the cluster. Honest attestations act like a vine over basalt: connected growth is rewarded, while isolated mass remains spectrally confined.
